short: A remarkably durable German battlecruiser that barely survived catastrophic magazine fires at Dogger Bank and massive flooding at Jutland.
full:
Commissioned on 22 May 1913, SMS Seydlitz was a German battlecruiser noted for her incredible survivability. At the Battle of Dogger Bank in 1915, a British shell pierced her aft turret armour, igniting cordite charges. The resulting fire flashed into the adjacent turret, killing over a hundred men. Only the quick flooding of her magazines prevented the ship from exploding entirely, prompting critical German improvements to ammunition handling.

She returned to fight at the Battle of Jutland in 1916, where she absorbed twenty-one heavy shell hits and a torpedo strike. Taking on over five thousand tons of water, she sank so low by the bow that she had to be steered backwards to port, but she successfully returned. She was scuttled by her crew at Scapa Flow in 1919.
